title: Dynamic Topology Quantum State Compression
abstract: Quantum state compression is a crucial task in quantum information science, aiming to reduce the number of qubits required while maintaining high fidelity. Static compression techniques often struggle with large datasets, necessitating dynamic approaches. This paper proposes a novel dynamic topology-based quantum state compression algorithm, leveraging the inherent properties of topological structures to achieve efficient data transfer. We present a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the topology of the quantum state, enabling targeted compression and optimization. The algorithm's core principle is the creation of a 'dynamic' topology that adapts to the input, resulting in improved compression ratios and reduced computational complexity compared to static methods. This work explores the potential of utilizing topological properties for efficient data manipulation within the quantum realm.

title: 基于动态自适应的动态图论优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-adaptive graph optimization algorithm designed to enhance model performance and accuracy through dynamic structural adjustments. Traditional graph optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. Our approach leverages a "dynamic graph structure" mechanism, continuously adjusting graph parameters based on data feedback and model error. This dynamic adjustment allows the algorithm to automatically refine the graph, mitigating the limitations of static optimization techniques. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss its potential applications across various modeling domains.

title: Temporal Data Causal Learning and Dynamic Graph Models
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of causal learning from time-series data, a problem frequently encountered in various domains such as healthcare, finance, and environmental science. Traditional causal inference methods often struggle to capture the dynamic nature inherent in temporal data, leading to inaccurate causal models. This work proposes a novel approach that combines structural causal inference (SCI) with dynamic graph models. The core idea is to learn causal relationships directly from time-series data using SCI and then represent these relationships within a dynamic graph structure that can evolve over time. We define a framework for incorporating temporal dependencies within the causal model, allowing us to represent and reason about dynamic causal pathways. The resulting dynamic graph model can then be used for prediction, intervention analysis, and understanding the underlying causal mechanisms driving the observed temporal patterns. We outline the key components of this framework and discuss its potential applications, highlighting the advantages of this approach over traditional methods. The paper culminates in a conceptual model and provides a foundation for future research in this area.

title: Adaptive Self-Differencing Functions
abstract: This paper investigates the design of an adaptive self-differencing function, aiming to enhance model prediction accuracy and stability by dynamically adjusting function parameters based on input data characteristics and computational error. We explore a novel approach utilizing adaptive parameter control during the calculation process to achieve a more robust and tailored model. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic parameter adjustment strategy that reacts to data feature variations and error propagation, resulting in improved predictive performance. The paper presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in addressing challenges encountered in predictive modeling.

title: Formal Semantic Networks: Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to intelligent system development centered around the adaptive optimization of formal semantic networks. The core idea involves leveraging the structural and relational information embedded within semantic networks to automatically generate efficient algorithms and programs. This is achieved by transforming the network into a formal logic representation, utilizing formal reasoning and optimization algorithms to uncover implicit knowledge and hidden relationships. The resulting algorithms and programs then enable the intelligent system to adapt and evolve autonomously. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology to reduce the complexity of artificial intelligence development by automating the process of algorithm design and self-improvement. The primary contribution lies in the integration of formal semantics with algorithmic optimization, leading to a system capable of self-generation and adaptive evolution. This approach aims to provide a framework for building more robust and intelligent systems by directly translating semantic understanding into executable code.

title: Title: Adaptive Graph Neural Network Knowledge Distillation
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive graph neural network (GNN) knowledge distillation method. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the parameters of the GNN to effectively transfer knowledge from a large model to a smaller model, thereby improving model efficiency and generalization ability. We propose a novel approach that incorporates a learning rate schedule for the GNN's parameters, allowing the model to adaptively adjust its structure to better match the target model. The method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in model efficiency and performance compared to existing knowledge distillation techniques.

title: A Novel Computation Architecture Based on Quantum Coherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computation architecture centered around the exploitation of quantum coherence. The core concept involves structuring a computational system to leverage the inherent parallelism afforded by quantum coherence, thereby aiming to significantly enhance computational efficiency compared to traditional architectures. We outline a framework where interconnected quantum systems operate in a manner that maximizes the duration of quantum coherence, allowing for parallel processing of multiple computational tasks simultaneously. The architecture is designed to mitigate decoherence effects, a primary challenge in quantum computing, through strategic system design and operational protocols. This approach represents a fundamentally new paradigm in computation, shifting from sequential, deterministic operations to a massively parallel, probabilistic one based on the quantum mechanical principles of superposition and coherence. The potential impact of this architecture extends across various fields, including scientific simulations, optimization problems, and machine learning, where the ability to process vast amounts of data concurrently offers a transformative advantage. ---

title: Quantization of String Operands
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum string operations as a foundation for a novel computational framework, specifically designed to accelerate the computation of string-based algorithms. We propose a method that transforms key string operation steps into quantum operations, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism centers on the strategic application of quantum algorithms to manipulate the fundamental structure of string calculations, offering a fundamentally new approach to this complex mathematical problem. The exploration of this framework addresses limitations inherent in traditional computational methods and holds promise for significant advancements in string theory research and related mathematical applications.

title: Leakage-Controlled Classification of Dataset-Derived Ordinal p53-Signature Size Categories in Fallopian-Tube Immunohistochemistry
abstract: Background and Objectives: p53 signatures are segments of strongly p53-immunoreactive secretory epithelium in the fallopian tube. We tested whether fixed pathology-pretrained image representations could classify three ordered categories reconstructed from the public dataset’s reported cell-count intervals. Methods: The primary cohort comprised 113 canonical p53 20× fields from 67 patients: 59 Small (12–20 cells), 24 Medium (21–80), and 30 Large (>80). A 141-field partial-label cohort retained boundary-spanning intervals for sensitivity analysis. Twenty-six eligible feature/head pipelines were evaluated by three-repeat five-fold nested patient-grouped cross-validation. Within every outer fold, the pipeline was selected using inner validation only; primary performance metrics were computed within each repeat and averaged across the three repeats, while the resulting 339 held-out predictions were pooled only for the confusion-matrix visualization. Uncertainty was estimated using 2000 patient-cluster bootstrap replicates conditional on these recorded predictions. Results: The fold-wise nested selector achieved quadratic-weighted kappa (QWK) 0.687 (95% CI 0.547–0.785), macro-F1 0.628 (0.568–0.680), balanced accuracy 0.637 (0.581–0.693), macro-AUROC 0.805 (0.750–0.855), and macro-AUPRC 0.681 (0.633–0.754). Small, Medium, and Large sensitivities were 0.870 (0.801–0.928), 0.264 (0.159–0.386), and 0.778 (0.617–0.906); severe Small–Large errors occurred in 6.5% (2.9–10.6%). Equal patient weighting gave QWK 0.700. In a secondary locked UNI2-h/CORAL analysis, ordinal temperature scaling reduced ECE from 0.195 to 0.157 and negative log-likelihood from 1.291 to 0.778. Conclusions: Fixed representations provided useful internal discrimination of dataset-derived ordinal categories, with substantial fold variability and weak Medium-category sensitivity. The results do not validate lesion measurement, detection, diagnosis, or clinical use; independent pathologist-annotated evaluation is required.

title: Anomaly detection in long-term time series with Transformer and variational autoencoder
abstract: Abstract Anomaly detection is crucial for ensuring system reliability and providing early warnings of potential failures. However, long-term time-series anomaly detection remains challenging because anomalous events are rare, anomaly patterns are diverse, and temporal dependencies can extend across multiple scales. Traditional methods and existing deep learning models still struggle to jointly represent fine-grained temporal variation, long-range contextual information, and the distribution of normal patterns. This work presents Transformer with variational autoencoder (TransVAE), a framework that combines a dual-embedding representation pipeline, a Transformer encoder for long-range dependency modeling, and VAE-based latent regularization of encoded features. Specifically, local position-aware embeddings and feature-wise global embeddings are integrated into a shared representation before attention modeling, and the VAE is applied to the Transformer-encoded representation to regularize the latent space of normal patterns. Evaluations on benchmark time-series datasets show that TransVAE outperforms several state-of-the-art baselines, achieving improvements in the area under the receiver operating characteristic by 6.7% and 13.6%, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity analyses further support the contributions of each component of the framework. These results demonstrate that TransVAE provides an effective and robust solution for long-term time-series anomaly detection.

title: Foundation Models for Generalizable Semantic and Goal-Oriented Communication
abstract: Semantic and goal-oriented communication is increasingly studied for 6G, but generalization beyond seen data remains a key weakness under tight rate budgets. Many existing systems overfit their training data and degrade sharply at very low bit rates because they attempt to compress the entire signal. We introduce Foundation Model-Guided Semantic and Goal-Oriented Communication (FMSGOC), a framework that uses broad visual-linguistic Foundation Model priors to mitigate overfitting. It further improves rate efficiency by concentrating bits on sparse, goal-aligned anchors and relying on generative foundation-model priors to reconstruct the masked regions. By decoupling what to send from how to reconstruct, a vision-language foundation model selects and transmits a sparse set of semantic anchors, while a pretrained diffusion model, fine-tuned for masked completion, reconstructs the image at the receiver. In our experiments, FMSGOC reaches 0.039 bits per pixel (BPP), maintains high semantic fidelity (cosine similarity 0.87-0.90 on CIFAR-10), remains robust on previously unseen inputs (0.83-0.86 on ImageNet), and shows good perceptual similarity (0.1278/0.1558, CIFAR-10/ImageNet), outperforming strong end-to-end baselines at lower bit rates.

title: Parallelism Strategy Chaining for Fast Training Convergence
abstract: Selecting a parallelism strategy - the configuration of data, tensor, and pipeline parallelism degrees together with micro- and global-batch sizes - largely determines the training efficiency of large language models. State-of-the-art methods search for a parallelism strategy offline and select the single strategy that minimizes per-iteration time. But we find that they neglect the target validation perplexity and time-to-perplexity (TTP). In particular, our analysis reveals that the best strategy yielding the fastest perplexity improvement changes multiple times during training. As a result, state-of-the-art methods are 1.8-11.4x slower in TTP than the strategy sequence that selects the best strategy at each iteration. This paper proposes CONA, a new training method that introduces online strategy chaining. Instead of a single strategy selected offline, CONA ranks candidate strategies during training using a surrogate metric built from compute throughput and gradient statistics, and switches the current strategy to a new strategy with a higher metric. In our evaluation with GPT-3 1.3B, BERT-Large, and Llama-3.2-1B, CONA reaches the target validation perplexity 1.4-9.6x faster than state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, CONA closely tracks the perplexity achieved by the sequence that selects the best strategy at each iteration, within 2.6%.

title: Progressive Pruning: Analyzing the Impact of Intersection Attacks
abstract: Stream-based communication dominates today's Internet, posing unique challenges for anonymous communication networks (ACNs). Traditionally designed for independent messages, ACNs struggle to account for the inherent vulnerabilities of streams, such as susceptibility to intersection attacks. In this work, we address this gap and introduce progressive pruning, a novel methodology for quantifying the susceptibility to intersection attacks. Progressive pruning quantifies and monitors anonymity sets over time, providing an assessment of an adversary's success in correlating senders and receivers. We leverage this methodology to analyze synthetic scenarios and large-scale simulations of the Tor network using our newly developed TorFS simulator. Our findings reveal that anonymity is significantly influenced by stream length, user population, and stream distribution across the network. These insights highlight critical design challenges for future ACNs seeking to safeguard stream-based communication against traffic analysis attacks.

title: Ontology matching evaluation : A statistical perspective
abstract: This paper proposes statistical approaches to test if the difference between two ontology matchers is real. Specifically, the performances of the matchers over multiple data sets are obtained and based on their performances, the conclusion can be drawn whether one method is better than one another or not. To do so, the paired t-test and Wilcoxon signed rank test are proposed and the comparisons over six recently proposed methods are reported. © 2016, CEUR-WS. All rights reserved.

title: AI元系统原生智能理论
abstract: 当前人工智能研究在语义接地、可解释性及能效方面遭遇根本性瓶颈,其深层根源在于将智能本质等同于高维统计拟合。本文提出元系统原生智能理论(MSɅIT),主张智能并非数据驱动的函数逼近,而是基于”主导-调制”二元操作的代数构造过程,其深层逻辑结构由第一性关系R₀生成,全部推理规则均可还原为R₀的有限次派生操作。 本文的核心贡献在于:(1)从认知发生学的操作闭包原则出发,论证六层基础认知范畴构成认知系统闭环表征的最小完备集合,其二元组合生成64维基础标签空间——64在此被定位为认知智能的必要基元数,而非宇宙的普遍常数;(2)严格定义第一性关系R₀的三层公理(主导约束Dom、调制约束Mod、不可逆约束¬Rev),并论证其在封闭推理系统内的逻辑必然性,同时明确其在开放系统中的弱化条件;(3)构建逻辑模态范畴L与C₅-集合范畴离散单点集骨架子范畴的函子等价,为模态推理提供范畴论的结构支撑;(4)将先验公理体系翻译为”只读定义域-可修改调制域”的分层架构工程规范,实现从形式理论到可执行约束的映射。 本文明确划定理论的适用边界:MSɅIT适用于具有清晰”定义域-调制域”分层的认知系统与AI推理系统,其公理体系在此边界内成立;在开放复杂系统中,¬Rev公理弱化为统计不可逆约束。64维空间的必然性被限定为认知操作闭包的基元数,而非跨越物理-生物-认知所有层级的普适常数。这一边界划定使理论具备清晰的可证伪性。

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Field Theory Quantum Computing Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing algorithm based on Adaptive Topological Field Theory (ATFT). The core idea of the algorithm is to leverage the unique properties of ATFT to enhance the simulation and optimization of quantum computations, thereby improving the efficiency and accuracy of quantum computing. We introduce a framework for dynamically adjusting the parameters of the ATFT to tailor the computational process to specific problems. The algorithm's design incorporates a novel approach to mapping quantum states onto the ATFT landscape, facilitating efficient exploration of the solution space. We explore the potential of this approach for tackling various quantum algorithms, specifically focusing on those benefiting from enhanced simulation capabilities. The research aims to advance the field of quantum computing by providing a practical and efficient method for optimization and simulation.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Topology and Quantum Computing: A Cross-Disciplinary Exploration
abstract: This paper investigates the intersection of nonlinear geometry topology and quantum computing, proposing a novel quantum computation algorithm predicated on a framework rooted in topological quantum information processing. The core claim is the development of an algorithm capable of achieving deeper control and measurement of quantum entanglement through the incorporation of self-linking and self-connectivity properties within a quantum qubit system. This advancement aims to significantly enhance the efficiency and computational capabilities of quantum computing by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The work presents a mechanism for establishing a quantum qubit system structured by topological principles, enabling enhanced entanglement manipulation and utilizing self-association properties to guide quantum computation. The investigation explores the potential for this approach to represent a significant shift in quantum algorithm design, moving beyond the limitations of classical qubit operations.

title: Dynamic Semantic Network Reasoning Engine (DSNRE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Network Reasoning Engine (DSNRE), a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning that addresses the limitations of traditional, static systems. The core claim is that integrating continuous, active semantic understanding modeling with knowledge graph inference processes enables adaptive, dynamic reasoning in response to evolving data and context. DSNRE employs a multi-layered feedback loop system comprised of a rule-based and probabilistic graph inference engine, a pre-trained language model-based semantic understanding module, an active query generation module, and a continuous learning module. The system iteratively refines its understanding and reasoning capabilities through proactive querying and continuous learning, achieving real-time adaptation to dynamic semantic changes. The key innovation lies in the deep integration of semantic understanding and inference, moving beyond static knowledge-based deduction to a more intelligent, self-aware system. This paper outlines the architecture, functionality, and theoretical underpinnings of DSNRE, highlighting its potential for applications requiring robust and adaptable reasoning in dynamic environments.

title: Nonlinear Topological Quantum Computing Adaptive Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive learning algorithm for nonlinear topological quantum computing (NTQC) based on self-organized quantum systems. Traditional machine learning approaches rely on pre-defined models, while this algorithm leverages the inherent adaptability of non-linear topological quantum systems. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting quantum system parameters to optimize performance in response to environmental changes. This approach offers enhanced scalability, flexibility, and potential for efficient quantum computation. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the algorithm's capabilities in a simplified model. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research.

title: 基于非对称性约束的概率图的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm for probabilistic graphs that leverages non-symmetry constraints to dynamically adjust graph structure, ensuring stability in optimization results. Traditional optimization methods often require manual design of the graph structure, which struggles to adapt to dynamic graph changes. This algorithm utilizes non-symmetry constraints to transform the optimization problem into a dynamic probability graph structure, enabling a more flexible and robust optimization process. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining the graph structure based on the input probability distribution, resulting in improved convergence and stability. This work presents a framework for adapting optimization algorithms to complex probabilistic graph environments.

title: Quantum Decoherence Control Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum Decoherence Control Theory aimed at enhancing coherence times in quantum states through precise environmental noise management. The core mechanism relies on analyzing the impact of environmental noise on quantum states, utilizing quantum information theory and noise theory foundations to design targeted control strategies. Specifically, the theory proposes feedback control and quantum error correction techniques to suppress noise propagation and extend coherence times. Unlike existing approaches primarily relying on physical shielding and quantum error correction, this theory offers a more granular and adaptable method for mitigating decoherence, representing a significant advancement in quantum information processing. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining key equations and control parameters, and demonstrating the potential for achieving significantly longer coherence times under controlled noise conditions. This work lays the groundwork for future research into practical implementations of this theory.

title: Quantum Adaptive Topology Optimization (QATO)
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Topology Optimization (QATO) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to leverage quantum self-adaptation principles to enhance the performance of quantum systems. This paper introduces a QATO algorithm that dynamically adjusts parameters within a quantum system to achieve optimal results, offering a significant departure from traditional optimization techniques. We detail the core mechanism, exploring how the quantum self-adaptation allows for the exploration of complex, multi-scale optimization landscapes, ultimately leading to improved system performance. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and experimental validation. The primary goal is to provide a robust and efficient method for optimizing quantum systems, potentially unlocking new capabilities and applications.

title: Meta-Learning for Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is a critical but often time-consuming step in the machine learning pipeline. Traditional methods like grid search and random search are inefficient, particularly for complex models and large search spaces. This paper investigates the application of meta-learning techniques to address the challenges of HPO. We propose a framework where HPO is formulated as a meta-learning problem, leveraging past optimization experiences to accelerate the learning process. Our approach aims to learn a meta-learner that can rapidly adapt to new model-dataset combinations, significantly reducing the HPO time. We demonstrate that meta-learning can effectively learn optimal hyperparameter configurations, leading to improved model performance compared to conventional HPO methods. The core claim is that meta-learning provides a mechanism for rapid and efficient hyperparameter tuning. The key mechanism is framing HPO as a learning problem and using meta-learning algorithms for training.

title: Probability Space Logic: Dynamic Topology Extension
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic topology extension in probability space logic to enhance data analysis and machine learning algorithms, particularly concerning high-dimensional datasets. We introduce a novel probabilistic space logic system built upon dynamic topology expansion, enabling automatic augmentation and improved computational complexity. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent flexibility of dynamic topology to handle complex data patterns. This approach promises to overcome the limitations of static logic systems in effectively processing high-dimensional data. The investigation focuses on the advantages and challenges of this dynamic topology approach, highlighting its potential impact on algorithm efficiency and data representation.

The core mechanism involves utilizing dynamic geometry topology for calculations and subsequently revealing underlying topological transformations. This approach offers a powerful and automated way to validate complex topological structures, potentially leading to breakthroughs in quantum information processing. The paper details the methodology, including the mathematical formulations and computational processes.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Particle Trajectory Optimization with Adaptive Constraints
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize particle trajectory optimization. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with dynamic constraints, hindering efficient trajectory design. We introduce a novel approach that leverages quantum algorithms to dynamically adjust constraints based on the particle's behavior, mimicking the adaptive mechanisms observed in biological systems. This integration of quantum principles offers a significant leap forward in optimizing particle trajectories, achieving enhanced performance and adaptability compared to traditional methods. The paper details the proposed methodology, including the quantum algorithm framework and a preliminary analysis of its effectiveness.

title: 可解释人工智能的因果推断引擎
abstract: This paper proposes a novel engine for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) focused on causal inference. The core claim is to construct an AI engine capable of performing causal reasoning and providing more reliable explanations for decision-making. The engine leverages a mechanism based on structural causal models, integrating Bayesian Networks and Deep Learning to identify and infer causal relationships, ultimately generating explainable decision processes. Traditional XAI methods often struggle to provide genuine causal explanations, limiting their utility in high-stakes decision scenarios. This work addresses this limitation by explicitly incorporating causal inference, significantly enhancing the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-driven decisions. The proposed system aims to move beyond simply explaining correlations to elucidating the underlying causal mechanisms driving outcomes. The system is designed to be modular and adaptable, allowing for the integration of diverse datasets and causal discovery techniques. Further research will focus on refining the explanation generation process and validating the engine's performance across various domains.

title: The Great Amnesia: AI Agent Memory as the Binding Constraint on Autonomous Systems in Enterprise and Defense
abstract: Every frontier laboratory is racing to make the system smarter. None is racing to make it remember. That is not a gap in the market. That is the market. Four years of capability gains have not moved the rate at which organisations put artificial intelligence into production. The industry reads that as an adoption problem. It is an architecture problem, and the evidence is already public. A frontier laboratory's own usage data shows computer and mathematical tasks at roughly 35 percent of consumer conversations and close to 44 percent of API traffic, with software error correction the single most frequent task: the most capable reasoning systems ever built, deployed overwhelmingly on work small enough to fit inside one session. Enterprise research puts pilot failure at approximately 95 percent and attributes it not to model quality but to a learning gap. Time-horizon measurement shows 50 percent horizons in hours against 80 percent horizons of roughly one. And long-horizon agent performance collapses from 40 to 50 percent down to below 10 percent when the same task is embedded in a longer history, with the required information still inside the context window. That last result settles the question. Not knowledge, not retrieval, not context length. Capability is compounding and continuity is not, and no quantity of parameters has ever fixed an architecture problem. The paper maps where every layer of the market sits relative to that gap, including Palantir, Anduril and Shield AI, shows defense buying the identical defect at scale, demonstrates why memory features, larger windows and retrieval each fail to close it, specifies the eight properties a continuity layer must hold, and issues an open two-cycle test that any laboratory, platform, prime or programme office can run against its own stack, and against the author's. Version 2.0 supersedes version 1.0. Companion preprint: Continuous Mission Intelligence: The Decisive Architecture for Command at Machine Speed, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22646255. The author is co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rebootix AI, Inc.

title: Adaptive Encryption Framework for Web Applications: A Risk-Based Approach to Dynamic Algorithm Selection
abstract: Web applications increasingly handle sensitive data in diverse use cases, but conventional encryption implementations apply a uniform level of cryptographic protection to all traffic, regardless of the associated risk. This static approach results in either excessive computational overhead when applying maximum encryption universally, or inadequate protection when using lightweight encryption to preserve performance. This paper proposes an Adaptive Encryption Framework (AEF) designed to bridge the gap between performance and security in web applications. Rather than relying on a static protocol, AEF dynamically adjusts encryption algorithms based on a real-time composite risk score (0–100). This score is derived from six weighted variables: network risk (25%), authentication strength (20%), behavioral risk (20%), device trust (15%), data sensitivity (15%), and temporal risk (5%). Depending on the calculated risk, the system automatically transitions between three distinct security tiers: GREEN (utilizing ChaCha20-Poly1305), YELLOW (AES-256-GCM), or RED (AES-256-GCM with per-request HKDF key derivation for key isolation). All three profiles use exclusively standardized cryptographic primitives. The proposed weighting distribution was evaluated through sensitivity analysis on 27 framework-executed scenarios and further calibrated using 40,000 labeled application requests. Within these experimental conditions, it achieved complete agreement with the expected scenario classifications, and no alternative weight configuration produced better held-out performance. Additional validation on 61,065 HTTP requests from the CSIC 2010 dataset yielded an area under the ROC curve (ROC AUC) of 0.860, with no attack request assigned to the lightweight profile under the evaluated operating conditions. Across three hardware platforms and four payload sizes, all encryption profiles maintained sub-millisecond latency. Extended load testing showed that a four-worker Node.js cluster sustained 4948 requests per second at 2000 concurrent connections, a 7.1-fold improvement over a single process. When hardware cryptographic acceleration was disabled, ChaCha20-Poly1305 became up to 9.1 times faster than AES-256-GCM, supporting its use as the lightweight profile. The framework proposed in this paper operationalizes the qualitative risk assessment guidelines from NIST SP 800-30 and SP 800-63 into a quantitative, automated encryption selection mechanism for web applications, evaluated under the hardware platforms, concurrency levels and traffic assumptions described in this study.

title: Dynamic obstacle avoidance method for 3D animation group based on multi-agent reinforcement learning
abstract: At the forefront of 3D animation, virtual reality and robotics, it is difficult to realistically and efficiently simulate the group behavior of a large number of people and objects. Previously, traditional rule-based or optimization-based methods often encountered critical problems such as local collisions, unnatural trajectories, or the inability to escape deadlocks—especially in complex, high-density, and dynamic environments. In addition, these old methods also have limitations in overall coordination and flexibility, as they typically rely on local optimal calculations that fail to account for global group dynamics, inevitably leading to deadlocks in high-density continuous control scenarios. To tackle these specific limitations, our proposed approach integrates a localized attention mechanism. By supplying the transformer encoding into a policy network, each “agent” effectively collects and filters information about nearby agents and dynamic obstacles, proactively anticipating collision threats to maintain global coordination. It is noteworthy that the proposed method utilizes a comprehensive reward function that balances obstacle avoidance, movement efficiency, and path fluency. We have fully tested this method called Attention-MAPPO for populations with low/high density, static/dynamic barriers in the Unity 3D modeling environment. The experimental results show that the average obstacle avoidance success rate of this method in all tasks is 92.6%, and the average movement time is 12.4 s. Compared with the baseline standard MAPPO, its success rate has increased by an average of 4.4%, and the average movement time has been shortened by 6.8%, showing significant performance improvement. Furthermore, ablation studies on the attention mechanism clearly demonstrate its crucial role in achieving optimal performance in highly complex dynamic environments. This study provides a powerful and scalable solution for a real, effective team simulation that has a big impact on interactive virtual environments, game development and intelligent robots.

title: The OCUDU dApp Platform: An Open Runtime and E3 Interface for Real-Time AI-RAN
abstract: Machine learning has shown its largest gains in the band below 10 ms inside a 3GPP new radio (NR) 5G distributed unit (DU): link adaptation, per-slot scheduling, channel estimation, and the receiver itself. No open platform has let independently built software run there. Prior dApp frameworks reached the band only as external observers of an export stream. This paper is a guided introduction to the OCUDU dApp platform, an open runtime and E3 interface under which signed AI-RAN applications execute inside a production DU under three timing contracts: resident on the GPU receive chain (Class A), inside the scheduler's 100 us admitted deadline (Class B), or as never-blocking observers whose results the scheduler consumes (Class C). The conventional path is never displaced, and every authority is typed, validated, and operator-bounded. The paper explains how the runtime, the embedded E3 agent, and the three public repositories fit together; shows a dApp's source, its signed package, and its lifecycle state machine; defines the contracts a module is written against; and shows how one management surface serves a Python script, an operator's console, and an LLM agent. On a GB10 gNB with attached handsets, dApps of all three classes, including an out-of-tree neural equalizer, ran together on a live cell without a single fallback, and equalizer variants were compared over the air by lifecycle operations alone. Every measured checkpoint is reported with its conditions and its gaps. Platform, SDK, and a zero-hardware quickstart are public under BSD-3-Clause-Clear as a preview release of the OCUDU AI-RAN Working Group 2, inviting feedback, new use cases, and independent vetting ahead of upstreaming into the OCUDU mainline.

title: Quantum Approximate Counting with Bernoulli Oracles
abstract: Quantum counting is a fundamental quantum algorithm that estimates the fraction of marked elements using a membership oracle, achieving a quadratic speedup over classical sampling. The membership oracle, however, assumes exact labeling of each element, but this assumption fails when the labels are inherently probabilistic. We study quantum counting with \emph{Bernoulli oracles}, where given $m$ Bernoulli distributions with unknown biases $p_1,\dots,p_m$ and a gap parameter $Δ$, the goal is to estimate the fraction $ρ$ of \emph{positive} distributions ($p_i\ge1/2+Δ$) to within additive error $ε$. We prove an upper bound of $\tilde{O}\!\big(\frac{\sqrtρ}{Δε}+\frac{1}{Δ\sqrtε}\big)$ queries, achieving a quadratic speedup over the classical sample complexity. % of $Θ(ρ/Δ^2ε^2)$. Our algorithm first uses the Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) to coherently amplify the bias gap without collapsing the superposition over distributions, and then applies two-stage adaptive amplitude estimation. We complement this upper bound with a near-matching lower bound of $Ω(\sqrtρ/(Δε))$ via a new composition theorem for the quantum adversary method in the Boolean-over-average-case direction. For the special case of a constant gap $Δ=Θ(1)$, which corresponds to the bounded-error oracle where each query returns the correct label with constant probability, our bounds specialize to $\tilde{O}\big(\frac{\sqrtρ}ε+\frac{1}{\sqrtε}\big)$ and $Ω(\frac{\sqrtρ}ε)$, thereby characterizing the query complexity of quantum counting with bounded-error oracles.

title: SeisBench DAS: A machine learning framework for Distributed Acoustic Sensing
abstract: Fibre optic sensing, such as distributed acoustic sensing (DAS), has become a widespread technology for geophysical studies. To process the large-scale datasets produced by DAS, several machine learning methods have been proposed. However, without standardization of data and models, these methods lack comparability and interoperability. This introduces a gap between model developers and practitioners analyzing DAS data and inhibits adoption of deep learning for DAS. To address these limitations, here we present SeisBench DAS, an extension to the SeisBench library for machine learning in seismology. SeisBench DAS defines standard formats for DAS benchmark datasets, including standardised metadata and labels, and DAS models. It builds on the xdas framework for data ingestion and virtual array handling, and on PyTorch for reading and applying the machine learning models. Importantly, SeisBench provides an engine to efficiently apply deep learning models to diverse formats of DAS data, bridging the gap between model developers and practitioners. SeisBench DAS is designed as an open and extensible framework, allowing to easily incorporate future developments in deep learning for DAS.

title: Measuring Prompt-Induced Instability in Large Language Model–Based Fact Verification.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to verify factual claims, yet the stability of their verdicts is rarely examined. We ask whether an LLM returns the same fact-verification label for the same claim when only the prompt phrasing changes, or even when nothing changes across identical repeated runs. We evaluate three frontier models (GPT-5.6, Claude Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.1 Pro) on 250 label-balanced FEVER claims, presented without evidence, under five semantically distinct prompt framings, each repeated five times, for a total of 18,750 predictions. Using paired statistics (paired bootstrap, exact McNemar) and bootstrap confidence intervals, we find that verdicts are not reproducible even at temperature 0 (86.7-93.3% determinism), that models differ significantly in stability, and that instability concentrates on the abstention (NOT ENOUGH INFO) decision rather than on factual reversals. We argue that stability must be reported alongside accuracy when evaluating LLM fact-checkers.

title: Lean 4 Confirmation and Approval Proof for Hamzah Equation. (55)
abstract:
بخش اول: مقدمه علمی و ضرورت دکترین ۱۱۵۵ بعدی حمزه در درمان جامع ۱۰ کیسِ تهاجمیِ سیستمِ تنفسی و مدیاستن (کدهای ۱۱ تا ۲۰) تومورهای تهاجمی سیستم تنفسی و مدیاستن (ازجمله SCLC پیشرفته، آدنوکارسینومای ریه با جهش EGFR، کارسینومای اسکواموس، LCNEC مدیاستن، مزوتلیومای پلور، کارسینومای تیمیک، سمینومای مدیاستن، آدنویید سیستیک تراشه، تیمومای مهاجم نوع C و بلاستومای ریوی) از پیچیده‌ترین و مخرب‌ترین چالش‌های انکولوژی قرن ۲۱ هستند. این بدخیمی‌ها با جهش‌های کلیدی نظیر MYC، EGFR، FGFR1، TP53، KRAS، BAP1، KIT و CTNNB1 باعث ایجاد «سرریز پهنای باند» (Bandwidth Overflow) و نشت اطلاعاتی در کلاک کروموزومی شبکه‌های بافتی ریه می‌شوند. روش‌های سنتی (شیمی‌درمانی و ایمنی‌درمانی کلاسیک) به دلیل نرخ بالای خطای پردازشی و هتروژنیته ساختاری در برابر این تومورها ناکارآمدند. مدل جامع مانیفلد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی ($\psi$–Hamzah) با تلفیق مکانیک لاگرانژی، مشتقات کسری کاپوتو، سد فلوکس صفر (Flux Barrier) و اصول هم‌ارزی چندلایه، بستری انقلابی برای شبیه‌سازی دقیق برهم‌کنش‌های دارو-هدف، پاکسازی نویزهای انکوژنی و باززایی سلولی در سراسر ۱۰ کیس تنفسی فراهم می‌کند. ۵ کد سطح امگا اولترا (Omega Ultra Advanced) برای ۱۰ کیس تنفسی و مدیاستن در مانیفلد ۱۱۵۵D ۱. کد اول پایتون: هسته جامع محاسباتی، داکینگ تانسوری انکوژن‌ها (MYC تا CTNNB1) و نگاشت‌های فانکتوری مانیفلد ۱۱۵۵D این موتور تخصصی مجهز به لایه‌های ضربه‌گیر ترمودینامیکی، محاسبه تانسور برهم‌کنش دارو-هدف (DTI) برای پروتئین‌های پاتولوژیک سیستم تنفسی، انرژی پتانسیل لنارد-جونز، فیلتر قانون لیپینسکی و پایش امتیاز پایداری فلوکس است. Python import datetime import logging import numpy as np import torch from typing import Any, Dict, List, Union logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='[%(asctime)s] [HAMZAH-RESPIRATORY-KERNEL] : %(message)s') class HamzahGrandUnifiedRespiratoryKernel: """ HamzahXcell: Grand Unified Computational Theory & Respiratory Oncology Manifold Engine (Omega Production Grade) Unifies Quantum Physics, Tensor Docking for Oncogenic Drivers (MYC, EGFR, CTNNB1, etc.), ADMET, and Bandwidth Control across 1155D. """ MANIFOLD_DIM: int = 1155 OMEGA_H_15: float = 2.3e170 EPSILON_FLOOR: float = 1e-15 def __init__(self, cluster_id: str = "Hamzah_Respiratory_Target_Omega_1155D") -> None: self.cluster_id = cluster_id self.integrity_score = 1.0 logging.info(f"Initializing Respiratory Grand Unified AI Engine for Cluster: {self.cluster_id} in {self.MANIFOLD_DIM}D.") def compute_docking_energy_grid(self, ligand_coords: List[float], receptor_grid: List[float]) -> Union[float, str]: """محاسبه تانسور برهم‌کنش دارو-هدف (DTI) و انرژی لنارد-جونز برای پروتئین‌های انکوژن تنفسی در مانیفلد 1155D""" if not ligand_coords or not receptor_grid: self.integrity_score -= 0.15 logging.error("خطای داکینگ تنفسی: مختصات لیگاند یا شبکه گیرنده پاتولوژیک تهی است.") return "ERROR: مختصات مولکولی نامعتبر است." lig = torch.tensor(ligand_coords, dtype=torch.float64) rec = torch.tensor(receptor_grid[:len(ligand_coords)], dtype=torch.float64) r = torch.norm(lig - rec) + self.EPSILON_FLOOR lj_potential = torch.sum(4.0 * 0.12 * ((1.0 / r)**12 - (1.0 / r)**6)) return float(lj_potential.item()) def filter_lipinski_rule_of_five(self, molecular_weight: float, log_p: float, h_donors: int, h_acceptors: int) -> Dict[str, Union[bool, str]]: """فیلتر پیشرفته قانون لیپینسکی برای ارزیابی نفوذپذیری بافتی و پایداری کلاک تنفسی""" passed = (molecular_weight <= 445.0) and (log_p <= 4.3) and (h_donors <= 4) and (h_acceptors <= 8) status = "PASSED_RESPIRATORY_LIPINSKI_OPTIMAL" if passed else "REQUIRES_STRUCTURAL_MODIFICATION" return {"Lipinski_Passed": passed, "Status": status} def quantum_chemistry_functor(self, orbital_electron_density: List[float], energy_potential: float) -> Union[float, str]: """نگاشت تابع موج کوانتومی به انرژی اتصال انکوژنی و مهار نشت پهنای باند در 1155D""" if not orbital_electron_density: self.integrity_score -= 0.15 return "ERROR: بردار چگالی الکترونی نمی‌تواند تهی باشد." clean_density = [max(0.0, float(d)) for d in orbital_electron_density] binding_energy = float(np.sum(np.array(clean_density, dtype=np.float64) * energy_potential)) return max(0.0, binding_energy) def run_grand_compliance_report(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: report = { "Timestamp": datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "Manifold_Dimension": self.MANIFOLD_DIM, "Omega_H_15": self.OMEGA_H_15, "Docking_Energy_Test": self.compute_docking_energy_grid([1.2, 3.3, 5.4], [1.1, 3.1, 5.3]), "Lipinski_Filter": self.filter_lipinski_rule_of_five(315.0, 2.2, 2, 5), "Quantum_Chemistry": self.quantum_chemistry_functor([1.4, 0.7], 2.85), "Grand_Unified_Status": "FULLY_OPERATIONAL_RESPIRATORY_AI_DRUG_DISCOVERY_1155D", "Integrity_Score": round(self.integrity_score, 2) } return report if __name__ == "__main__": kernel = HamzahGrandUnifiedRespiratoryKernel() report = kernel.run_grand_compliance_report() print("
--- گزارش انطباق هسته جامع محاسباتی سیستم تنفسی (1155D) ---") for k, v in report.items(): print(f"{k:<35} : {v}") print("
[HAMZAH-XCELL] هسته مانیفلد تخصصی تنفسی با موفقیت مستقر شد.") ۲. کد دوم پایتون: موتور تانسوری توزیع‌شده، انحنای ریچی و اعتبارسنجی ADMET در مانیفلد سیستم تنفسی (HamzahDistributedManifoldTensorEngine) این سیستم از هندسه گراف NetworkX و پردازش تانسوری موازی با دقت torch.float64 برای تحلیل انحنای ریچی، شاخص‌های ایمنی ADMET و سد فلوکس صفر در سراسر مانیفلد ۱۱۵۵D بهره می‌برد. title: Dynamic Adaptive Markov Random Field (GMM)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Dynamic Adaptive Markov Random Field (GMM) algorithm designed to handle data distributions that evolve over time. Traditional GMMs often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively model dynamic data patterns. This work proposes a method for dynamically adjusting model parameters based on observed data fluctuations, thereby enabling robust and adaptable modeling across various datasets. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously updates the model's parameters to best fit the evolving data distribution. We present a comprehensive analysis demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and experiments, showcasing its capacity to maintain high accuracy while adapting to changing data characteristics. The results highlight the significant advantages of this dynamic GMM approach over static models in scenarios requiring real-time data adaptation.

title: Computational Complexity Analysis of Quantum Algorithms using Category Theory
abstract: Traditional methods for analyzing the computational complexity of algorithms, predominantly rooted in classical computer models, struggle to accurately characterize the potential advantages offered by quantum computation. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing category theory to provide a more fundamental and abstract framework for assessing the complexity of quantum algorithms. Instead of focusing on the specifics of quantum hardware, we examine the underlying categorical structures that define the computational processes inherent in these algorithms. This allows us to identify and analyze complexity properties that are independent of the physical implementation. We define key concepts like quantum states as objects and quantum gates as morphisms, establishing a formal connection between quantum computation and category theory. This framework facilitates a more rigorous and generalized understanding of quantum complexity, potentially revealing new insights and providing a basis for comparing different quantum algorithms. The core claim is that traditional complexity analysis is inadequate, and the mechanism is the application of category theory for a more abstract and generalized framework.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Computation
abstract: Quantum state adaptive computation (QSAC) offers a fundamentally new approach to quantum computation by introducing a self-adjusting mechanism within quantum circuits. This mechanism allows the quantum state to dynamically modify its properties during computation, enabling the execution of complex, non-linear operations beyond the capabilities of classical algorithms. This paper explores the design and implementation of a QSAC model, detailing its core mechanism, advantages, and potential impact on the field of quantum computing. We present a conceptual framework demonstrating the potential for QSAC to unlock new computational possibilities and push the boundaries of quantum information processing.

title: Non-Local Quantum Computing Based on Adaptive Geometric Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-local quantum computing framework centered around adaptive geometric optimization. We propose a quantum algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve significantly enhanced precision in computations compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism involves strategically manipulating entangled states to induce specific geometric transformations within the quantum system, enabling the algorithm to find optimal solutions with higher fidelity. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement in the realm of quantum computation, particularly in applications requiring high precision and complex optimization problems. We present a detailed theoretical analysis, including the mathematical formulation of the optimization process and the implementation of the core algorithm. The resulting algorithm demonstrates superior performance in a series of benchmark tests, highlighting its potential for revolutionizing various fields, including materials science, drug discovery, and financial modeling.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing framework based on adaptive topology transformations. Traditional quantum computing approaches often rely on fixed, static transformations, limiting their expressiveness and computational power. Our framework leverages dynamically adjusted topological transformations, enabling precise and efficient manipulation of quantum states through the application of quantum entanglement. We detail the core mechanism of this framework, emphasizing the dynamic nature of the transformations and their potential to significantly enhance computational capabilities. The proposed method offers a fundamentally new approach to quantum algorithm design and optimization, promising improved performance in complex quantum simulations and quantum state manipulation. We provide a detailed mathematical model and discuss the implications for future research and development in the field of quantum computing.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Emergent Phenomena
abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic quantum simulation to unlock insights into complex, emergent phenomena. We investigate the design of an algorithm capable of modeling flocking, convection, and other systems exhibiting self-organization through quantum mechanics. The core claim is that this approach, leveraging quantum algorithms, will provide unprecedented predictive power and allow for the discovery of novel patterns and behaviors within these systems. The paper details the chosen quantum algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the simulation of a simplified flocking example. We will discuss the challenges and opportunities associated with this research, highlighting the potential impact on fields ranging from materials science to biology.

abstract: This paper presents a novel iterative algorithm for optimal network design, specifically tailored for applications in machine learning. The algorithm's design is driven by the need to balance computational cost with the potential for achieving superior performance within a constrained environment. The paper details the algorithm's structure, the constraints employed, and a demonstration of its effectiveness through a specific machine learning task. The focus is on a robust and adaptable approach suitable for a range of network design scenarios.

abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization strategy for matrix operations based on quantum topology. Traditional matrix operations often rely on classical algorithms, and this research explores the potential of quantum topology to enhance efficiency and uncover underlying patterns within these calculations. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent topological properties of matrices to guide the optimization process, resulting in improved computational performance. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating a quantum state representation that mirrors the matrix's structure, allowing for efficient search and refinement of the matrix's values. This approach aims to minimize the computational cost while potentially revealing previously unknown mathematical relationships. The paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method.

title: 基于量子纠缠的分布式传感器网络数据融合
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to data fusion within distributed sensor networks leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. Traditional sensor network data fusion methods often suffer from centralized processing, leading to vulnerabilities such as single points of failure and communication delays. This research introduces a system where multiple quantum sensors, interconnected through quantum entanglement, perform distributed data synchronization and fusion. The core claim is that this approach enhances data accuracy and reliability. The mechanism relies on the inherent correlations provided by entanglement, enabling real-time data alignment and intelligent aggregation without the limitations of centralized architectures. We outline the theoretical framework, explore the key mathematical formulations, and discuss the potential benefits and challenges of implementing such a system. The system's adaptive and dynamic nature represents a significant departure from conventional sensor network data fusion techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Nonlinear Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement simulation framework designed to model complex non-linear quantum systems. The core focus is on developing an algorithm that dynamically manipulates quantum entanglement, enabling the simulation of intricate physical phenomena and revealing underlying behavior patterns. The study leverages high-precision computational models to achieve accurate and detailed simulations. This work addresses limitations of existing simulation techniques by providing a unique approach to quantum system modeling. This paper presents the design and implementation of the "Quantum Entanglement Perturbation Field" algorithm, which dynamically alters the entanglement state to mimic the behavior of complex physical systems. We explore the potential of this framework to generate more accurate and insightful representations of quantum physics. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this research for advancing our understanding of quantum phenomena.

title: Non-Spin State Quantum Entanglement Generation and Control
abstract: This paper investigates the generation and control of quantum entanglement utilizing non-spin states, specifically photons and atomic nuclei, aiming to overcome the limitations inherent in spin-based entanglement approaches. The core claim centers on leveraging alternative physical systems to create and manipulate entanglement. The proposed mechanism explores the utilization of strong nonlinear optical effects and nuclear quantum state interactions to achieve non-spin entanglement. Precise pulse control is then employed to actively manage and manipulate these entangled states. The research contributes to a broader understanding of quantum resources and offers more flexible control methodologies. This work explores the potential of non-spin entanglement for advanced quantum technologies. The key mathematical framework relies on the formalism of quantum mechanics, specifically utilizing the density matrix representation to describe the state of the entangled system. We introduce the concept of entanglement fidelity as a metric for evaluating the quality of the generated entanglement. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future experimental investigations into non-spin quantum entanglement.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Matrix Reconstruction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to a novel matrix reconstruction algorithm. The core claim is the development of an adaptive matrix reconstruction method predicated on the inherent correlations of entangled states, allowing for a more intelligent and robust reconstruction process than traditional methods. We introduce a '纠缠度量' parameter to dynamically adjust the entanglement strength and shape, optimizing the reconstruction for specific input matrices. The algorithm leverages the instantaneous correlation between entangled particles to perform matrix transformations without requiring explicit computation. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings of the algorithm, describes the implementation of the core mechanism, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in reconstructing complex matrices. We explore the impact of the '纠缠度量' parameter on reconstruction quality and stability.

abstract: This paper investigates the intricate interplay between multi-particle quantum entanglement and its topological structure. We explore how the inherent properties of entanglement, particularly its topological nature, can significantly influence quantum information processing, offering a novel framework for understanding and optimizing quantum computation. The study focuses on analyzing the effects of topological entanglement on quantum gate operations, ultimately proposing a method leveraging topological structure for enhanced quantum information handling. The core claim is that by understanding and leveraging the topological properties of multi-particle quantum entanglement, we can achieve more efficient and robust quantum systems.

title: Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Dynamic Edge Refinement
abstract: Existing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) often struggle to effectively model dynamic graphs where relationships between nodes change over time. This research introduces a novel framework, Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Dynamic Edge Refinement (TGDENR), designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to represent graph edges as time-series data, enabling the use of recurrent neural networks or transformers to dynamically refine edge weights based on temporal dependencies. A novelty detection function is employed to identify edges exhibiting significant deviations from established patterns, further enhancing the model's adaptability. The proposed method offers a robust solution for analyzing evolving graph structures, particularly relevant in domains such as social networks, financial markets, and biological systems. The model's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, paving the way for future experimental validation.

title: Rancang Bangun Chatbot Customer Service Multi-Tenant Berbasis Large Language Model Menggunakan Context Stuffing
abstract: The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), has transformed customer service into a more automated, adaptive, and responsive system. However, LLM-based chatbots still face several challenges, including hallucination, limited capability to serve multiple organizations simultaneously, and difficulties in website integration. This study aims to design and develop an embeddable multi-tenant customer service chatbot based on a Large Language Model. The system was developed using the Go programming language, Fiber framework, PostgreSQL database, and a JavaScript widget that can be embedded into company websites using a single line of code. The Research and Development (R&D) approach was adopted, while the context stuffing method ensured that chatbot responses were generated only from each tenant's official knowledge base, thereby minimizing hallucination. The evaluation included black-box testing, response accuracy measurement, hallucination assessment, response time analysis, and tenant data isolation testing. The experimental results demonstrated that the chatbot achieved 100% response accuracy for in-domain questions, produced zero hallucination for out-of-domain questions, maintained an average response time of approximately four seconds, and successfully preserved complete data isolation among tenants. Furthermore, the chatbot widget was easily embedded into company websites with minimal configuration. These findings indicate that the proposed chatbot provides an effective, secure, and scalable AI-based customer service solution suitable for multiple organizations.

title: Quantitative image feature integrated digital pathology model based on deep learning and machine learning for binary histological severity stratification of ulcerative colitis
abstract: The STRIDE II consensus recognizes histopathological healing in ulcerative colitis as a key therapeutic target. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate a quantitative image-based model for the binary classification of mild versus moderate-to-severe UC based on histopathological features. Pathological slides from 167 ulcerative colitis patients (58 mild, 109 moderate-to-severe) were retrospectively collected from two medical centers. A U-Net model quantified glandular structures (number, area ratio), Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix analyzed texture features, and a five-interval grayscale histogram was modeled. Features selection was performed using LASSO regression. Patients were randomly divided into training and test sets in a 7:3 ratio. Machine learning models were constructed and their performance was evaluated. In the five-fold cross-validation analysis within the training set, SVM achieved the highest mean ROC-AUC and was selected as the final model. After refitting on the full training set, the final SVM model achieved an AUC of 0.891 (95% CI: 0.742–0.958), a sensitivity of 0.848 (95% CI: 0.691–0.933), a specificity of 0.833 (95% CI: 0.608–0.942), and an F1-score of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.774–0.952) on the independent test set. SHAP analysis identified gland area ratio, fibrosis, and GrayHist_100_149, defined as the proportion of mucosal pixels with intermediate grayscale intensity ranging from 100 to 149 in grayscale-converted H&E images, as the most important predictors. This study integrated glandular geometry, texture features, and grayscale analysis using machine learning to develop a quantitative auxiliary tool for the binary stratification of mild versus moderate-to-severe UC. These findings suggest that this approach may serve as a complementary approach for histological assessment in ulcerative colitis.

title: Survey of Novel Deep Learning Architectures for Denoising Gravitational-wave Signals
abstract: Gravitational-wave denoising must handle the full diversity of spinning, precessing binaries, since the recovered waveform underpins parameter estimation, tests of general relativity, and population studies. Matched filtering achieves this at a cost that becomes prohibitive as next-generation detectors push event rates higher; deep learning offers real-time reconstruction, but current methods are developed on narrow parameter spaces, precluding principled comparison and reliable deployment. We present the first controlled comparison of five neural-network architectures for gravitational-wave denoising, trained identically across the full astrophysically-motivated spinning binary-black-hole parameter space. A unifying principle emerges: matching network structure to the spectral anatomy of a coalescence -- inspiral, merger, ringdown -- outperforms brute-force model scaling. Our Multi-Scale Frequency-Aware architecture embodies this via dedicated parallel branches per frequency regime, achieving the best fidelity while using fewer parameters than larger models. It generalizes from simulated training to real LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data without retraining, recovering merger morphology across confirmed events spanning three observing runs and both detectors, despite training on a single detector's simulated noise. We construct population-level uncertainty bands from denoising residuals, validate their calibration, and stress-test the framework on extended mass ratios and a spin population resembling hierarchical-merger remnants. Applied to real noise with no known signal, the network suppresses its output almost everywhere, with rare exceptions traced to noise transients rather than a general weakness -- indicating the statistic discriminates signal from noise and motivating a future detection study. Released weights give a deployable, reproducible benchmark for future extensions.

title: Heat Kernel Textures: the Geodesic Gaussians That Do Not Splat
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting has recently revolutionised novel view synthesis as well as many other 3D vision methods and applications. Drawing inspiration from this representation, we now rethink textures to overcome the main issues of UV mapping while considerably lowering their memory footprint. Heat Kernel Textures (HKTex) eliminate UV unwrapping as well as their persistent issues of wasted UV space, seams, distortions, vertex-duplication, and varying resolution. Grounded in discrete Riemannian geometry and intrinsically defined on any manifold surface discretised as a triangular mesh, HKTex uses anisotropic heat kernels as geodesic equivalents to Gaussians. Like our kernels, also the optimisation of their position and the adaptive densification strategies were redefined to operate on the surface of the object to be textureised. Our novel representation is also fully integrated with a physically based renderer and can be optimised either from existing textures or multi-view images. Our project page and code are available at circle-group.github.io/research/HeatKernelTextures.

title: 2-Fold Forrelation is in QAC$^0$
abstract: We show that 2-fold Forrelation with inverse-polylogarithmic promise gap can be solved, with bounded error, by polynomial-size QAC$^0$ circuits. Unlike the standard oracle-based Forrelation algorithm, our circuits receive the input explicitly, in the same form as the AC$^0$ circuits against which Forrelation is known to be hard. At constant gap, this yields a natural promise-problem separation between QAC$^0$ and AC$^0$.

title: A Hybrid Grey Wolf and Dipper-Throated Optimizer for Engineering Design Optimization
abstract: Optimization plays a fundamental role in engineering design, enabling cost reduction, performance enhancement, and constraint satisfaction.Metaheuristic algorithms such as the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Dipper-Throated Optimizer (DTO) have been widely used for solving complex optimization problems.However, standalone algorithms often suffer from premature convergence and limited exploration capabilities, necessitating the development of hybrid approaches.This chapter introduces a novel hybrid algorithm, GWO+DTO, which combines the exploratory strength of GWO with the exploitative efficiency of DTO to improve optimization performance.The effectiveness of GWO+DTO is evaluated on two benchmark engineering problems: the Pressure Vessel Design Problem and the Tension/Compression Spring Design Problem, comparing its results with standalone GWO and DTO.Experimental findings demonstrate that the hybrid approach achieves superior performance, obtaining the best cost of 5950.28 in the pressure vessel problem and 0.01266 in the spring design problem, outperforming the individual algorithms in accuracy and efficiency.Additionally, GWO+DTO requires fewer function evaluations, highlighting its computational efficiency.The proposed hybrid method presents a promising alternative for tackling real-world engineering optimization challenges, with potential applications in multi-objective and large-scale optimization problems.

title: Biological Reservoir Computing in Modular Human iPSC-Derived Neuronal Networks
abstract: Introduction While human brain mapping characterizes these relationships at the macroscale, advancements in Synthetic Biological Intelligence (SBI) now allow us to investigate them in controllable, human iPSC-derived neural systems [1]. To systematically probe these mesoscale dynamics, we utilized the CL1 platform, which facilitates high-level programmability of in vitro networks, allowing for precise spatiotemporal electrical stimulation and real-time functional readouts. Treating cultures as physical reservoirs, we ask whether enforcing modular connectivity (segregation + integration) enhances separability of neural state trajectories compared with unstructured 2D monolayers, across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal classification benchmarks. Methods In this work, human iPSC-derived cortical and hippocampal neurons were cultured as 2D monolayers or in 60-module PDMS microfluidic devices enforcing modular connectivity coupled by a peripheral loop enabling re-entrant paths. Spikes were recorded on CL1 at 25 kHz; stimulation/noise artifacts were removed via waveform PCA + GMM clustering. We tested reservoir encoding with spatial source discrimination, Morse 'S' vs 'O' sequence decoding, and MNIST driven as 16-channel, 5-step spiking tensors. Spike counts were binned to form state vectors x(t) and decoded by logistic regression with 5-fold CV, against shuffled and test-chip controls. Results All biological cultures supported above-chance spatial decoding, but modular devices improved fidelity, with mixed cortical–hippocampal modular networks reaching ~96% median accuracy (Fig.1). Temporal Morse decoding depended on network dynamics: only highly active modular cultures outperformed shuffled controls, while hippocampal monolayers were near chance. For MNIST, monolayers performed poorly, whereas high-activity modular cultures achieved 69–75% median (max 82–88%) accuracy; shuffled and test-chip controls stayed at chance. PCA of reservoir states revealed class-separable manifolds only in real modular data. Discussion While physical Reservoir Computing has been demonstrated in non-biological substrates, its validation in human iPSC-derived neural networks remained limited [2]. In this work, we show that human iPSC neuronal cultures can act as robust biological reservoirs, and enforced modular topology functions as a computational regularizer that expands functional dimensionality and supports fading memory for complex spatio-temporal separation. The synergy of biological identity (hippocampal + cortical) and engineered modular connectivity suggests a programmable route to test how structural constraints enable—or impair—computation, with implications for both SBI applications and mechanistic models of dysconnectivity in brain disorders. Treating cultures as physical reservoirs, we ask whether enforcing modular connectivity (segregation + integration) enhances separability of neural state trajectories compared with unstructured 2D monolayers, across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal classification benchmarks. Methods In this work, human iPSC-derived cortical and hippocampal neurons were cultured as 2D monolayers or in 60-module PDMS microfluidic devices enforcing modular connectivity coupled by a peripheral loop enabling re-entrant paths. Spikes were recorded on CL1 at 25 kHz; stimulation/noise artifacts were removed via waveform PCA + GMM clustering. We tested reservoir encoding with spatial source discrimination, Morse 'S' vs 'O' sequence decoding, and MNIST driven as 16-channel, 5-step spiking tensors. Spike counts were binned to form state vectors x(t) and decoded by logistic regression with 5-fold CV, against shuffled and test-chip controls. Results All biological cultures supported above-chance spatial decoding, but modular devices improved fidelity, with mixed cortical–hippocampal modular networks reaching ~96% median accuracy (Fig.1). Temporal Morse decoding depended on network dynamics: only highly active modular cultures outperformed shuffled controls, while hippocampal monolayers were near chance. For MNIST, monolayers performed poorly, whereas high-activity modular cultures achieved 69–75% median (max 82–88%) accuracy; shuffled and test-chip controls stayed at chance. PCA of reservoir states revealed class-separable manifolds only in real modular data. Discussion While physical Reservoir Computing has been demonstrated in non-biological substrates, its validation in human iPSC-derived neural networks remained limited [2]. In this work, we show that human iPSC neuronal cultures can act as robust biological reservoirs, and enforced modular topology functions as a computational regularizer that expands functional dimensionality and supports fading memory for complex spatio-temporal separation. The synergy of biological identity (hippocampal + cortical) and engineered modular connectivity suggests a programmable route to test how structural constraints enable—or impair—computation, with implications for both SBI applications and mechanistic models of dysconnectivity in brain disorders. title: Dynamic Chaos Optimization via Quantum Potential Landscapes
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic chaos optimization framework based on quantum potential landscapes. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle with complex, non-linear systems due to the limitations of classical methods. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum potential landscapes, which exhibit dynamic and spatially varying energy states, to guide optimization processes. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum potential landscape that dynamically adjusts to the system's state, promoting efficient solutions and minimizing errors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations of a chaotic system, showcasing improvements in performance metrics such as convergence speed and solution quality. The potential landscape provides a mechanism for self-organization and adaptation, leading to enhanced optimization outcomes. The study also explores the impact of varying the landscape's parameters on the optimization process. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this quantum-inspired optimization technique.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Bayesian Networks for Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning that explicitly addresses the critical challenge of uncertainty quantification. Current neuro-symbolic systems often lack a principled way to represent and manage uncertainty arising from both the neural network component and the symbolic reasoning engine. We introduce a framework that integrates Bayesian Networks (BNs) with a symbolic reasoning system, allowing for the probabilistic modeling of neural network outputs and subsequent inference based on this uncertainty. The core mechanism involves constructing a BN to represent the uncertainties inherent in the neural network's predictions. This BN is then utilized as the knowledge base for a symbolic reasoning engine, enabling inferences while providing a quantifiable measure of confidence in the resulting conclusions. Our approach offers a robust solution for incorporating probabilistic reasoning into neuro-symbolic architectures, leading to more reliable and explainable AI systems. The proposed method significantly advances the field by providing a concrete solution to the long-standing problem of uncertainty in neuro-symbolic reasoning. The primary contribution lies in the systematic integration of Bayesian Networks within a neuro-symbolic framework, offering a tangible method for quantifying uncertainty throughout the reasoning process. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy.

title: Fractal Code Generation via Iterated Self-Similarity
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing fractal algorithms for software code generation. The core concept revolves around generating complex software architectures through iterative self-similarity, mirroring the patterns observed in natural fractals. The proposed methodology involves defining a base code module and repeatedly applying a transformation function – akin to the generation of the Mandelbrot set – to create progressively intricate code structures. This approach offers a novel systematic method for software design, potentially resulting in more efficient and adaptable code solutions. The research focuses on the underlying mathematical principles driving this fractal generation process, establishing a theoretical framework for its application in software development. Key metrics for evaluating the generated code's complexity and efficiency are also discussed. This work represents a significant step toward a new paradigm in software design, moving away from traditional, monolithic approaches towards more adaptable and self-similar systems. ---
